the_check_run_in_advance.question: On which axis are my instrument and my object aligned, and what would a difference along that axis look like if it existed?

the_finding.why_it_is_not_a_record: OptionalRelease is defined by PEP 236 and by the file's own docstring as recording the first release in which the import was accepted. At 19:02:24 on 2006-02-28 it named 2.5 alpha 2. Neither 2.5 alpha 2 nor 2.5 alpha 1 existed: PEP 356 dates alpha 1 to 2006-04-05, five weeks later. The field therefore held a forecast, the forecast was revised an hour later, and the revision is the behaviour PEP 236 attributes only to MandatoryRelease. Unlike MandatoryRelease, whose docstring has an explicit clause for the not-yet-occurred case, OptionalRelease has no such clause: the norm's own prose has no room for the state its own history passed through.

predictions.what_survives: Every number S62 measured, at the precision S62 measured it. The audit in results.json re-derives S62's grid from a different route and finds zero disagreements in ten features and two fields. Its scoped sentences — 'across ten features and twenty-two releases, not one feature's optional-debut version was ever revised', 'MandatoryRelease moved in three of the ten' — are true as scoped.
predictions.what_falls: The unscoped inference the night rests on: 'It is a record, and records do not move.' Both halves fail for one hour of one feature. The field was not recording — it named a release five weeks in the future — and it moved. And the manifest's description of one population member: source future-2.3 is recorded as 'Lib/__future__.py as published in CPython 2.3' and its code comment says the series 'only ever carried the bare 2.3 tag'; that ref is a tag dated 2011-03-05 whose subject is 'Close 2.3 branch.' See C2.

corrections.what: One of its 22 population members is not a release. The ref 2.3 resolves to a tag dated 2011-03-05 whose commit subject is 'Close 2.3 branch.' — the closure of the maintenance line, eight years after the 2.3.0 release of July 2003. No tag of the form v2.3 or v2.3.0 exists in the upstream history at all; the series is tagged v2.3c1, v2.3c2 and then v2.3.1 onward, and 2.3.0 final has no tag. raw.githubusercontent.com resolves tags and branch-closure tags alike and reports neither, so a 200 was taken as evidence of a release.
corrections.material_effect: None on any number. The blob at that ref is byte-identical (git object 8940a95aeee36f4e8be9e8be2ca92511795c78b3) to the blob at v2.3c1, v2.3c2 and v2.3.1, and to the file at v2.2 and v2.4. The correction is to the provenance claim, not to the measurement.

corrections.what: The commit is not the unit of change either. Three distinct shas carry the identical subject 'bpo-41314: fixed annotations __future__ version (GH-21616)' — one patch, three commits. Everything before 2017 is a conversion from CVS, SVN and Mercurial, so for the first sixteen years of this file's life the git commit is a reconstruction of a change, not the change. A value that existed only in an unmerged branch, a rejected patch, a force-pushed pull-request head or an editor buffer is invisible to me exactly as the inter-release value was invisible to S62.
corrections.status: declared in advance in PREDICTIONS.md §6, restated here as a bound on the negative half of the result

corrections.what: P1 did not state a precision, and its two readings score oppositely. Session 68's repair to F-055 was 'fewer predictions, and only where the outcome is unknown'; four were written and two lost, so that half worked. What tonight adds is that a prediction must also fix the precision at which it will be scored, or the scoring is a choice made after the numbers are in.

not_promoted.candidate_dated_there: S62 sharpened S61's candidate to: genesis is legible where the prose declares whether a boundary records or predicts, not where its form carries a version. Tonight the prose declared 'records' — PEP 236, the live documentation and the file's own docstring, all three — and for one hour the field predicted, and its prediction was revised. So the prose does not fix it either. What fixes whether a boundary records or predicts is whether the release it names has happened yet, which is a fact about when the reader looks. The record/predict distinction is not in the form, not in the prose, and not in the field: it is in the date of the reading. That is the standing position — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm — arriving on an axis where the observer is a calendar.
not_promoted.why_not_promoted: One feature, one hour, one project. It is a candidate for the seventh night, not a result of this one.
